headline: 100,000 new health workers: PM Tarique Rahman outlines vision for 'healthy Bangladesh'
summary: The Prime Minister announced plans to recruit 100,000 additional health workers and 25,000 professional midwives to strengthen community-based primary healthcare.
details: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman announced a vision for a 'healthy Bangladesh' where healthcare begins at home and in the community, focusing on primary health care as the core of national health reform.
Speaking at a UN event in New York, the PM outlined plans to recruit 100,000 additional health workers, 80% of whom will be women, to connect families with the health system and identify risks early.
A key part of the strategy is the recruitment of 25,000 professional midwives across the country to provide essential reproductive care, support safe childbirth, and facilitate referrals.
The Prime Minister noted that Bangladesh now has over 11,000 licensed midwives, with a goal to reach 25,000 by 2030, supported by partnerships with Sweden and UNFPA.
The government is also developing an integrated digital health ecosystem, including Health Cards for every citizen linked to digital health records and electronic referral systems.
The vision for women's health extends beyond pregnancy to cover adolescent health, reproductive health, family planning, and the early detection of cervical and breast cancers.
The PM emphasized that the next phase of health reform will be driven by national ownership and sustainable domestic investment to ensure every woman has access to a skilled midwife close to home.
caption:
100,000 new health workers and 25,000 midwives. Bangladesh is transforming its health system to bring care directly to your doorstep.

Prime Minister Tarique Rahman announced a vision for a 'healthy Bangladesh' where healthcare begins at home and in the community, focusing on primary health care as the core of national health reform.

Speaking at a UN event in New York, the PM outlined plans to recruit 100,000 additional health workers, 80% of whom will be women, to connect families with the health system and identify risks early.

A key part of the strategy is the recruitment of 25,000 professional midwives across the country to provide essential reproductive care, support safe childbirth, and facilitate referrals.

The Prime Minister noted that Bangladesh now has over 11,000 licensed midwives, with a goal to reach 25,000 by 2030, supported by partnerships with Sweden and UNFPA.

The government is also developing an integrated digital health ecosystem, including Health Cards for every citizen linked to digital health records and electronic referral systems.

The vision for women's health extends beyond pregnancy to cover adolescent health, reproductive health, family planning, and the early detection of cervical and breast cancers.

The PM emphasized that the next phase of health reform will be driven by national ownership and sustainable domestic investment to ensure every woman has access to a skilled midwife close to home.

headline: Bangladesh and Pakistan premiers discuss bilateral ties at UN
summary: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman and Pakistani PM Shehbaz Sharif met at the UN headquarters to discuss regional cooperation and mutual interests.
details: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman of Bangladesh and Prime Minister Muhammad Shehbaz Sharif of Pakistan held a bilateral meeting on Thursday during the 81st session of the UN General Assembly.
The meeting took place on the 34th floor of the UN headquarters' Secretariat Building in New York.
The two leaders engaged in constructive exchanges regarding bilateral relations, regional and international situations, and potential areas of cooperation for the welfare of their people.
Both Prime Ministers emphasized advancing the relationship between the two nations based on mutual respect, understanding, and cooperation.
The meeting concluded with both parties agreeing to maintain regular communication and dialogue on matters of common interest.
caption:
A high-level diplomatic meeting in New York: Bangladesh and Pakistan's Prime Ministers discuss the future of their bilateral ties.

Prime Minister Tarique Rahman of Bangladesh and Prime Minister Muhammad Shehbaz Sharif of Pakistan held a bilateral meeting on Thursday during the 81st session of the UN General Assembly.

The meeting took place on the 34th floor of the UN headquarters' Secretariat Building in New York.

The two leaders engaged in constructive exchanges regarding bilateral relations, regional and international situations, and potential areas of cooperation for the welfare of their people.

Both Prime Ministers emphasized advancing the relationship between the two nations based on mutual respect, understanding, and cooperation.

The meeting concluded with both parties agreeing to maintain regular communication and dialogue on matters of common interest.
